classification.difficultyReason: Infer quadrant radius from symmetric total width and path width, then combine four quarter-circle areas; select given information and a short familiar geometric calculation.

content.prompt:
Clive has a square area of garden with side length $5\text{ m}$. He is planning to design a vegetable garden with two straight paths, each of width $1\text{ m}$, across the garden. The paths are to be at right angles to each other, as shown. The diagram is symmetric. He also plans to make four vegetable garden beds in the shape of quadrants, as shown, and to put pavers in the rest of the garden.

What will be the value of the area of the vegetable garden beds once the paths and pavers have been laid? Give your answer in square metres, in terms of $\pi$.

spec.description: Symmetric5m square, central perpendicular1m paths, four shaded quadrant beds and unshaded corner pavers. Bed radii not given as calculated labels.
spec.mathematics: Symmetric5m square, central perpendicular1m paths, four shaded quadrant beds and unshaded corner pavers. Bed radii not given as calculated labels.
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens and meaningful marks only; no calculated answers.

answer.worked: Each quadrant has radius $\frac{(5-1)}{2}=2\text{ m}$. Four quadrants make one complete circle, so the total bed area is $4\times\frac14\pi(2)^2=4\pi\text{ m}^2$.
